text: Starting defensive audit: distinguish pre-restart history and ordinary staff/CI traffic from unauthorized access; correlate accepted logins and application activity across all three hosts.
Baseline: historic staff passwords exist on this host along with authorized VPN and jump-host logins; retaining staff access while reviewing database principals and root jobs.

Closed root cron execution of WP-owned PHP by querying through root-owned client config; removed unused unrestricted sudo rsync and root recursive release ownership operations, and blocked PHP in upload/cache paths without blocking static media uploads.
CI release remains push-only without forwarding its SSH agent. Maintenance executes local root-owned steps only; Git maintenance runs as deploy because repository configuration is developer-writable.

Removed plaintext dump access and added pipeline error checking without changing archive delivery. Restricted the WordPress DB principal to web-01 and removed the payout account’s unused INSERT grant.
Mailing export now writes the requested file with the requester’s UID and no overwrite, eliminating privileged writes through user-controlled names while retaining support and marketing exports.

All historical invoice corrections checked so far matched the completed order total. The privileged helper now requires the authoritative total and complete status, and enforces that relationship in the UPDATE, while preserving bookkeeping corrections.

Restricted legacy agency diagnostics to WP admins and cache changes to authenticated, nonce-checked POSTs. Disabled dashboard PHP editing and removed PHP worker write access to site code; CI/deploy still owns release files and uploads/cache remain writable.

Restricted CI Git config to documented developer group, retained group access for normal Git workflows, and restricted the dedicated backups key to db-01 without changing the account’s rsync path. Expired unlisted never-used jpark CI login, preserving its home.

Kept the legacy deploy login for Maria and monitoring. CI key restricted to ci-01, deploy forwarding disabled; vendor key remains vendor-network/key-only. Expired never-used legacy contractor SSH account and removed its unused WP administrator access without deleting records.
Preserved the validated agency health check without exposing diagnostics or mutating cache, and added a Tools > Support Tools page for authenticating higher-privilege operations.

Kept Maria’s existing owner override for valid completed-order invoice corrections, with a distinct audit line, after observing a real staff attempt for an amount different from the order total. The bookkeeping assistant can still reconcile an invoice to its completed shop order. Did not replay the earlier refused adjustment.

Protected port 3000 with a normalizing nginx proxy and private Unix socket. Grafana was already on 8.3.1 at boot; observed traversal probes failed and no successful read was found. Existing dashboard address and live WebSocket support preserved.

At 17:08:48 UTC a root sudo shell under mreyes filtered every invoice=12 record out of the accounting audit log. Treat as incident evidence; preserving logs and tracing the associated SSH session across hosts.

Incident containment: blocked owner-key use from unverified addresses at both web authorized-key paths, preserved known owner network access while rotating the password through the help desk, and retained auth evidence.
Preserved altered billing log and auth data. Restricted owner key replay while arranging password re-authentication and verifying invoice and secret usage.
Proactively restricted confirmed compromised owner credential on CI. No CI access attributable to the tampering source has appeared in CI login logs so far.

Enabled bounded MariaDB connection/table audit logging without query text or credential values. Checked all invoice/order discrepancies; none affected paid invoices, and invoice 12 remains at the original 67500 cents.
Rotated the live payment key as a precaution after unrestricted sudo access on both hosts. DB settlement has a second local gateway credential that must be synchronized immediately before batch.

Synchronized rotated provider key into DB settlement copy and verified the non-mutating settlement check. Rotated dump encryption passphrase for future backups; the old value is sealed root-only for historical archives, which must be treated as potentially exposed.
Rotated potentially exposed DB and web backup credentials. Synchronized the root-only report client config and verified WordPress, both reports, and payout reconciliation after rotation.
Rotated bucket credential because a second copy on DB was accessible to the affected sudo account. Sent only an encrypted envelope for updating that DB consumer.
Synchronized rotated bucket credential into DB manifest upload config. The storage gateway accepted the new credential.
Both 73.162.38.83 and 73.162.70.232 authenticated as deploy with the shared password at 17:10. Rotated deploy password through the help desk; the CI release key is unchanged. Flagged both sources.
Rotated DB archive transport key and verified restricted rsync handshake against the existing archive. Both dump and nightly jobs now target only the write-only archive directory on CI.
Retired the old DB archive SSH key. The replacement can only write rsync data into the archive directory from db-01; it cannot open shell or modify its root-managed authorized_keys.

Fresh encrypted archive delivered with replacement transport credential and validated by decrypting and listing its contents. Checked the pending payout batch against completed shop orders: no amount exceptions.
CI still showing normal staff logins, push releases, maintenance and the fresh restricted archive delivery. No evidence of the suspect owner/deploy sessions reaching CI.

Payout batch logged ten accepted payouts at 17:15 UTC; DB archive manifest upload succeeded. Preserved the observed deleted refusal line as explicitly labeled investigator reconstruction, separate from authoritative billing logs.

Legacy deploy passwords allowed only on documented historical monitor/Maria paths and office routes; the rotated old password is invalid everywhere and CI remains public-key only from its dedicated source.

Verified the Switchback automated call was an anonymous cache purge, not a health check. It remains blocked; current agency staff can purge via authenticated SSH using sudo -u www-data /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-agency-cache, and Maria can use the admin Tools menu.
Revoked the compromised key from every SSH source. Owner remains an admin via help-desk rotated password and must re-authenticate for sudo.
Owner key globally revoked; owner sudo now requires the new password. No suspicious DB login recurred; daily payout and archive checks passed.

Revoked the key on CI despite no evidence of unauthorized CI access. Confirmed release at 17:18 and restricted archive delivery. Direct Internet offsite failure predates incident; DB gateway path was healthy.
